rv.q: The gag rate is breathtaking and the songs are bangers.
This show could be just what the West End needs.
This is a show that can movingly celebrate the unsung women of the secretarial pool while also allowing them to express their frustrations in a perfectly choreographed Beyoncé pastiche.
I’d wager, all the same, that this inventive gem of a night is in with a very good fighting chance of resounding victory.
This gloriously inventive musical, based on a celebrated Second World War intelligence operation, is the nearest thing to those hyperactive Tex Avery cartoons.

So too does this boundlessly inventive show constantly set its ambitions seemingly beyond its resources (including a cast of five summoning numerous characters) — and somehow not just meet but exceed them.
A brilliant spy thriller, a brilliant comedy, and a brilliant musical all rolled into one, it is exhilarating to see it hit the West End.
It more than delivers, and stands a shining example of homegrown talent

It is also one of the surprise survivors of the pandemic-stricken theatre. A show that looked like a caper with a cult following is on the brink of commercial success. Operation Mincemeat has moved into the Fortune theatre, haunted for more than 30 years by The Woman in Black.
This joyous spoof musical splices the two together, bringing vaudevillian flair to an irreverent telling of the story.
The show is witty, mocking, camp and joyous, not to mention immensely tuneful – the songs are both clever and catchy.
Really, it's a delight from start to finish.
The aim may have been to make a dumb musical but there is nothing dumb about this cleverly written and flawlessly executed production.
If you see one musical this year, make that Operation Mincemeat, the unlikely diamond of the West End.
They have written a true gem of a show, which highlights the importance of fringe theatre and its ability to nurture bold and creative storytelling.
It is that combination of heart, along with all the madcap tomfoolery preceding it, that encourages one to hope that Operation Mincemeat will be a West End resident for some time to come.
It’s guaranteed to give your ability to grin and giggle a strenuous, much needed workout.
Operation Mincemeat is pure joy from start to finish, and a wonderfully unique addition to the West End.
Mission Complete: Operation Mincemeat is the wittiest, most exciting, and most fun show in the West End right now.
This is an absolute must-watch.
The show is a riot of wonderful moments and quite irresistible. My advice is don't resist.
Compared with the lumbering, over-produced and lazily conceived jukebox musicals cluttering up the West End, this is a cluster bomb of creativity that raises the game.
Operation Mincemeat is the ultimate example of what amazing musical theatre can be.
